t.E905.agn: JECFA had set a group ADI of 20 mg/kg body weight/day for mineral oils, paraffins and microcrystalline waxes. In 2013 EFSA stated that, unlike mineral oil products, microcrystalline wax does not accumulate in tissues and that there is no concern for genotoxicity; as long-term studies were not available, it did not set an ADI, but found the margin of safety at the authorised uses sufficient.
t.E905.body: Intestinal absorption of hydrocarbons decreases as chain length increases; straight-chain paraffins longer than 30 carbons are very poorly absorbed.
t.E905.found.0: Surface of melons, papayas, mangoes, avocados and pineapples
t.E905.found.1: Confectionery (excluding chocolate), chewing gum, decorations and coatings
t.E905.prod: Obtained by refining petroleum or natural gas.
t.E905.regx.0: Re-evaluated; no ADI set, no safety concern at the authorised uses.
t.E905.summary: A petroleum-derived wax. Used as a coating on cheese rinds and chewing gum.
t.E905.what: A refined hydrocarbon wax chemically close to mineral oils; used for surface treatment.
